newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as prospects remain grim.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as prospects remain grim.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures recorded new losses on Monday, driven by grim chart signals and improving crop prospects.
Traders and analysts maintained a bearish stance towards the market, expecting benchmark May cocoa to chase support at 847 stg, a level dating from July 1995.
"It's looking on the weakish side," said one trader.

The session's turnover of 7,201 lots mainly centred on switches as players rolled positions forward. Early on, Ivorian offers on new crop contracts pressured the market after a weak opening and these were mainly absorbed by industry buying.

May finished the day five stg down at 882 stg a tonne and was above an intraday low of 876 stg. Analysts said the contract low of 871 stg (an 18-month low on second month continuation) looked vulnerable and could soon be put to test.
On the switches, March/May traded at 22, March/July at 41-42 and May/Dec at 55 with Phibro as the buyer. The distant March/May traded at 14 stg.
Traders cite large West African arrivals which show no sign of tailing off and a perception that the Ivorian midcrop could be surprisingly high as a result of favourable weather.
But they also blamed sterling which reversed cocoa's fortunes after a rally to 938 stg when it strengthened against the dollar and European currencies.
